title: What shapes the result
odia:
ଓଳି ଗୁଣେ କୋଳି
ପଲମ ଗୁଣେ ସରୁ ଚକୁଳି।
literal_meaning: The berries take their quality from the soil; the thin chakuli takes its quality from the pan.
meaning_odia: ମାଟି ଗୁଣେ କୋଳି ଓ ପଲମ ଗୁଣେ ଚକୁଳି ହେବାର ଉପମାରେ ଯେଉଁ ପରିବେଶରେ କିଛି ଗଢ଼େ, ତାହାର ପ୍ରଭାବକୁ କୁହାଯାଇଛି। ଦେଖାଯାଇଥିବା ସଂକଳନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହାକୁ ପିଲାଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ପିତାମାତାଙ୍କ ପ୍ରଭାବ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ।
explanation: The couplet pairs the ground in which berries grow with the pan on which chakuli is made. Both images connect a result to what helps shape it. The inspected compilation applies that comparison to parents and children; here it is read as an image of formative influence, not a fixed judgement of a child from their family.
usage_example: A discussion about children’s habits turns to the examples adults set at home. The saying could introduce the influence of that environment. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: ପଲମ is an earthen pan and ଚକୁଳି a flat cake; ସରୁ draws attention to thinness. The two compact comparisons bring cultivation and cooking together before the source gloss applies them to family influence.

graphic.caption: An imagined pairing places growing fruit beside chakuli in its pan, echoing the verse's formative influences.
